note: Single source of truth for clauses. The section 6 table in CAB-FREE-SPACE.md is GENERATED from this file by tools/clauses.mjs - do not edit that table by hand. Every 'authority' marked unverified must be resolved before sign-off: a clause without a cited source is an opinion with a reference number.

id_rules.immutability: An ID is a permanent public contract. It may appear in a customer report. Never renumber and never change what an ID means. Bump the minor version for clarification that cannot change an outcome; issue a NEW id and deprecate the old one for any change that can.
id_rules.deprecation: Deprecated clauses remain in this file with status deprecated and superseded_by set, so historical findings stay resolvable.

severity_scale.critical: Present risk of equipment damage, thermal shutdown or service loss.
severity_scale.major: Requirement breached with a real consequence, but no immediate risk.
severity_scale.minor: Requirement breached with limited consequence, or good practice missed.
severity_scale.info: No breach. Recorded for transparency about how the assessment was made.

clauses.title: Measured cabinet height must match the cabinet type record
clauses.requirement: The rack height measured from the image shall equal the total_u recorded for the cabinet type in site data.
clauses.rationale: A mismatch means either the wrong cabinet type is recorded or the scale estimate is wrong. Either way every derived figure is untrustworthy, so the assessment must not proceed.

authority.note: Not externally mandated; it is an integrity check on our own measurement.

clauses.remedy: Confirm the cabinet type in site data, then re-assess. If the record is correct, the scale estimate failed and the image should be re-taken.
clauses.false_positive_notes: Cabinets modified in the field (extension bays, plinths) will mismatch legitimately. Expect a real rate of these.

clauses.title: Scale must derive from the rail hole pattern
clauses.requirement: Pixels-per-U shall be established from the periodic mounting hole pattern, not from an assumed cabinet height.
clauses.rationale: The hole pattern is dimensionally fixed by EIA-310 at 15.875/15.875/12.7 mm, so it is a ruler present in every image. Deriving scale from an assumed height instead propagates any cabinet-type error into every measurement.
clauses.remedy: Re-shoot with both mounting rails fully in frame along their entire height.
clauses.false_positive_notes: Cabinets with covered or non-standard rails cannot satisfy this and will always abstain. Identify these cabinet types early.

clauses.title: Unclassifiable hardware counts as occupied
clauses.requirement: Any rack unit containing hardware that cannot be classified shall be counted as occupied, never as free.
clauses.rationale: Fail closed. Treating unrecognised objects as empty space produces the one genuinely dangerous error in this system: a full cabinet reported as having room.
clauses.remedy: Confirm installed equipment against the site record. If it is a known model, add it to the equipment catalogue so future assessments classify it.
clauses.false_positive_notes: A rising rate of this finding means new hardware has entered the fleet. Monitor it as a drift signal.

clauses.title: Occluded units are never counted as free
clauses.requirement: Rack units whose state cannot be determined shall be excluded from free_u and reported separately as occluded_u.
clauses.rationale: An occluded unit is unknown, not empty. Counting it either way is a guess; excluding it and widening the uncertainty interval is honest.
clauses.remedy: Provide a close-up of the obscured region, or dress cables clear of the rack face.

clauses.title: Open units in an airflow path require blanking panels
clauses.requirement: Rack units with no equipment installed, in an active airflow path, shall have blanking panels fitted.
clauses.rationale: Unblanked openings let cooled supply air bypass equipment and allow hot exhaust to recirculate to intakes, raising intake temperature across the whole cabinet rather than only at the opening.

authority.note: MUST cite the governing thermal or installation specification before sign-off.

clauses.remedy: Fit blanking panels to all open positions. No equipment change required.
clauses.false_positive_notes: Cabinets with bottom-to-top airflow may have different requirements than front-to-back. Confirm whether this clause is airflow-design dependent.

clauses.title: Minimum top clearance above units that require it
clauses.requirement: Equipment specified as requiring top clearance shall have the specified number of free rack units directly above it.
clauses.rationale: Top-vented equipment starved of clearance throttles or shuts down. This is a present risk, which is why it outranks free space in the decision table.

authority.source: TBD - product CPI per equipment model
authority.note: Needs the real product list and the clearance figure for each. Cannot be authored generically.

threshold.note: Placeholder. Must come from per-product CPI.

clauses.remedy: Relocate the unit above, or relocate the affected equipment, to restore the specified clearance.
clauses.false_positive_notes: Depends on correct equipment identification. A misclassified model yields a wrong clearance requirement.

clauses.title: Cable bundles must not obstruct available units
clauses.requirement: Cable bundles shall not obstruct rack units that would otherwise be available for installation.
clauses.rationale: An obstructed unit is not usable capacity even though it is empty, and the obstruction also prevents assessment of what lies behind it.

authority.note: Their existing field data records bundles consuming ~40% of cabinet free space as a recurring root cause; find the governing cable management spec.

clauses.remedy: Dress the bundle into the side cable manager so the positions become both usable and assessable.
clauses.false_positive_notes: Severity is interpretive, so this clause will have a higher override rate than the deterministic ones. Track it.

clauses.title: Available units must meet minimum usable depth
clauses.requirement: Rack units counted as usable shall provide the minimum usable mounting depth.
clauses.rationale: Front-plane availability does not imply installability. Depth is the most common reason a nominally free unit cannot take equipment.
clauses.remedy: Verify depth on site before committing to an installation plan.
clauses.false_positive_notes: Not determinable from a single frontal image. This clause exists to state that limitation explicitly rather than let a U figure imply installability.

clauses.title: Free units without spare power positions are not expansion capacity
clauses.requirement: Reported free rack units shall not be presented as expansion capacity unless spare power positions are confirmed.
clauses.rationale: A cabinet with ten free units and no spare breakers cannot take new equipment. Reporting the U figure alone invites a wrong capacity conclusion.
clauses.remedy: Confirm spare breaker positions from the power record or a dedicated photograph of the power compartment.

clauses.title: Serviceability clearance at the cabinet face
clauses.requirement: The cabinet face shall remain accessible for installation and maintenance work.
clauses.rationale: Equipment that cannot be safely reached cannot be serviced, which converts a simple fault into a longer outage.

authority.note: Likely covered by a safety or installation standard.

clauses.remedy: Clear obstructions from the working area at the cabinet face.
clauses.false_positive_notes: Only partially observable from a frontal image; floor-level obstructions are often out of frame.

clauses.title: Decommissioned equipment occupying rack space
clauses.requirement: Equipment recorded as decommissioned shall not remain installed.
clauses.rationale: Harvested from an existing recurring field root cause: legacy equipment not removed during upgrades, occupying capacity that is then reported as unavailable. This is recoverable space that no amount of cabinet planning will find unless it is named.

authority.source: Field root-cause data, Site AI Analysis

clauses.remedy: Schedule removal. Reclaimed units become available capacity at no cost.
clauses.false_positive_notes: Requires a reliable decommissioning record to join against. Without that this clause cannot be evaluated.
clauses.candidate_note: Not active. Demonstrates harvesting a clause from recorded field root causes rather than inventing one. Needs the decommissioning data source confirmed.

clauses.title: Cabinet approaching total capacity
clauses.requirement: A cabinet exceeding a stated occupancy fraction shall be flagged for capacity planning.
clauses.rationale: Harvested from a recurring root cause: unplanned additions taking cabinets to ~95% capacity with no space assessment. A threshold turns this from a post-hoc explanation into an advance warning.

authority.source: Field root-cause data, Site AI Analysis

clauses.remedy: Raise a capacity planning item before the next expansion is scheduled for this site.
clauses.candidate_note: Not active. Most valuable once change detection across visits exists, since the trend matters more than the snapshot.
